name: coordinator-feedback-routing
body:
The coordinator-mediated feedback protocol — no Rust control flow changes, because the `apg review` subcommand surface is unchanged. It spans every prose surface that describes or drives the cycle:

- Distributed agent prompts (`opencode-suite/agents/*.md`). The `codebase-navigator` prompt gains the feedback-action grant (`apg_review_action`) and the prose: dispatch one feedback item at a time to one plan/spec/implementer writer, receive the writer's ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claim, perform a shallow consistency check (ACTIONED with no change, or WONT-FIX with changes, is inconsistent), then action the item (`apg_review_action --fix|--wont-fix`) or re-dispatch it, leaving the terminal resolve/reject to the reviewer. The writer prompts (spec-writer, plan-writer, the generated implementer, and every test-implementer the agent-builder scaffolds) drop the action grant, hold a read-only feedback channel (`apg_review` — the spec-writer and plan-writer gain the read channel; the implementer already has it), and state that the writer returns a claim and never actions. The reviewer prompts (spec-review, plan-review, implementation-phase-reviewer) keep add/resolve/reject, never action, and have their cycle diagrams re-pointed (today `spec-review.md` / `plan-review.md` show `writer: apg_review_action … → actioned`).
- Suite tool text (`opencode-suite/tools/apg_review_action.ts`): its description is re-pointed from the writer to the coordinator.
- This repo's generated agents (`.opencode/agents/implementer.md`, `.opencode/agents/implementation-phase-reviewer.md`), regenerated by agent-builder; the agent-builder template re-points the grant shape for both the implementer and each test-implementer it scaffolds — none holds `apg_review_action`, each holds the read-only feedback channel.
- Rust doc-comment wording describing the cycle: `src/review_cmd.rs`'s module doc (lines 1-5) and the `review_action` doc (lines 243-244) say the writer actions it; re-point to the coordinator. Behavior is unchanged — the `apg --help` header and the five-verb dispatch line stay as-is (pinned by `help_text_documents_strict_surface_and_preserves_review`), consistent with `requirements.requirement.review-surface-unchanged`.
- Repo docs describing the cycle (AGENTS.md / README.md "writer↔reviewer feedback cycle" wording), re-pointed at the coordinator-mediated cycle.

Anchoring (delivery semantics): the durable delivered artifact is the embedded text plus its install path, not the repo-tree source file. The agent prompts and suite tool text are `include_str!` constants compiled into the binary and written to the user-level suite by `apg.install_suite`, so the `implemented-by` spine anchors to the install/embed Rust (`apg.install_suite`, `apg.main`) and the review CLI action path (`apg.review_cmd.review_action`). This is a DELIVERY-semantics choice, not a claim that those files are unscannable. TypeScript is already a scanned language: every `opencode-suite/tools/*.ts` is a File node with `code_type src` (e.g. `opencode-suite/tools/apg_review_action.ts`). Markdown becomes a scanned language under `requirements.requirement.markdown-frontend`: once `.md`/`.markdown` are accepted, `opencode-suite/agents/*.md` enter the graph as File/section nodes. The code-FQN universe keys off Module/Struct/Function/File records with no `status` set (src/main.rs:1342-1364), independent of file extension, so a scanned `.ts` or `.md` File FQN is a LEGITIMATE `implemented-by` target — the anchor deliberately stays on the embedding/install Rust because the embedded constant is what the installer delivers (see `solution.note.markdown-anchoring` / `solution.note.embedded-template-anchor`). The AGENTS.md/README cycle wording is repo documentation, not a distributed artifact, so it contributes no delivery anchor of its own.
